findings.body:
**Packet fields are read more than once, which breaks the single-read invariant from Lines 315–325.**

The dependency block says each value is read exactly once. That is not true in two places:

- `src/ops/review/internal/addressVerification.ts:346` reads `supplied[index]` again after reading the descriptor. If `supplied` is a Proxy, `getOwnPropertyDescriptor` can return a clean data descriptor while the `get` trap returns a different record. Use `descriptor.value` instead. Line 339 also re-reads `supplied.length` on every loop iteration.
- Line 271 keeps the live `packet.metadata.revision` object. `pinned` then reads `revision.head` and `revision.parent` again, and the returned `revision` stays live. `packet.patch`, `before`, `after` and `finding.text` are read again in `complete`, `coherent` and `trigger`. If `after` is accessor-backed, it can return content that matches the patch at Line 439 and drops the span at Line 485. That would produce a false `resolved`.

Snapshot these fields once into plain locals, and copy `{ head, parent }`, before the checks run.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix for the array slot</summary>

```diff
-          entries.push(supplied[index]);
+          entries.push(descriptor.value);
```
</details>





Also applies to: 346-346

findings.body:
**Distinguish quoted names from surviving triggers.**

In `src/ops/review/internal/addressVerification.ts:484-500`, any quoted text found in `before` causes `unresolved` if it remains in `after` or a cited dependency. For example, a fix can remove `"PARTIAL_MODE"` while retaining the quoted function name `"load"`; the name alone does not show that the defect survived.

Return `uncertain` when the evidence cannot distinguish a quoted name from the defect. Preserve `unresolved` when the cited trigger itself survives. Skipping every span outside a removed line would also skip unchanged defective code.
findings.title: Distinguish quoted names from surviving triggers.
